rust_declaration.source_context: 724: /// 725: /// Calculates the length of an Option<[String]> as an Option<[usize]> 726: /// without moving the [`String`]. The [`map`] method takes the `self` argument by value, 727: /// consuming the original, so this technique uses `as_ref` to first take an `Option` to a 728: /// reference to the value inside the original. 729: /// 730: /// [`map`]: Option::map 731: /// [String]: ../../std/string/struct.String.html "String" 732: /// [`String`]: ../../std/string/struct.String.html "String" 733: /// 734: /// ``` 735: /// let text: Option = Some("Hello, world!".to_string()); 736: /// // First, cast `Option` to `Option<&String>` with `as_ref`, 737: /// // then consume *that* with `map`, leaving `text` on the stack. 738: /// let text_length: Option = text.as_ref().map(|s| s.len()); 739: /// println!("still can print text: {text:?}"); 740: /// ``` 741: #[inline] 742: #[rustc_const_stable(feature = "const_option_basics", since = "1.48.0")] 743: #[stable(feature = "rust1", since = "1.0.0")] 744: pub const fn as_ref(&self) -> Option<&T> { 745: match *self { 746: Some(ref x) => Some(x), 747: None => None, 748: } 749: } 750: 751: /// Converts from `&mut Option` to `Option<&mut T>`. 752: /// 753: /// # Examples 754: /// 755: /// ``` 756: /// let mut x = Some(2); 757: /// match x.as_mut() { 758: /// Some(v) => *v = 42, 759: /// None => {}, 760: /// } 761: /// assert_eq!(x, Some(42)); 762: /// ``` 763: #[inline] 764: #[stable(feature = "rust1", since = "1.0.0")]
